aboutGame.title: What is The Eternal Abyss?
paragraphs: The Eternal Abyss is a high-difficulty Roblox tower obby created by developer bLockerman666. You spawn into a namesake main hub of 42 towers, step through portals to begin each climb, and work your way up obstacle courses that are built to punish rather than welcome you. The game's own description is blunt about it: losing progress and getting frustrated are expected parts of the experience, not bugs.

The challenge extends well beyond the starting hub. Branching zones such as Pit of Misery, Timeless Manor, and Starry Night each carry their own visual style and difficulty curve, and the developer's stated goal is to eventually host 50 towers in every area. Community difficulty charts, tier lists, and practice places have grown around the game to help climbers choose the right tower and drill the sections that keep ending their runs.

modules.name: The Eternal Abyss Beginner Guide
modules.description: New player guidance covering the main hub layout, portal system, checkpoint behavior, and early progression so beginners know exactly where to start in The Eternal Abyss.

highlights.detail: Scout the main area and walk the whole portal ring before you commit to any climb.
Start with the single Non-Soul Crushing tower in the 42-tower hub, since it lets you respawn instead of wiping the attempt.
Learn where each checkpoint resets your position, momentum, and camera before you push a full run.
Use a practice place to drill the room that keeps ending your attempts.
Warm up on a tower you have already cleared before you try a new one.

highlights.label: Practice
highlights.detail: Practice places rebuild tower segments so you can repeat one room with nothing on the line.

highlights.label: Rush
highlights.detail: A tower rush chains several towers into one continuous, no-reset endurance session.

highlights.label: Healing
highlights.detail: The healing tool restores your run after a bad jump or hazard hit, but it is balanced around scarcity.

highlights.label: Hints
highlights.detail: Portal hints and route notes fill the information gaps the game deliberately leaves open.

highlights.label: Secrets
highlights.detail: Tower secrets reward players who step off the main route to explore.

highlights.label: Reset
highlights.detail: Checkpoints restore your position but not your momentum, so the seconds after a reset decide the run.

highlights.label: Main Hub
highlights.detail: The namesake starting area holds 42 towers, and only one of them is Non-Soul Crushing.

highlights.label: Misery
highlights.detail: Pit of Misery carries its precision-heavy concept over from the Eternal Towers of Hell lineage.

highlights.label: Starry
highlights.detail: Starry Night pairs a night-sky theme with brutally hard climbs.

modules.name: The Eternal Abyss Tower Walkthrough
modules.description: A step-by-step walkthrough of how a The Eternal Abyss climb is structured, from reading the tower name and warning tag to surviving the final floors.

highlights.detail: Read the tower's name and portal warning tag before you enter, since both telegraph the gimmick.
Treat your first attempts as reconnaissance and memorize the timing of each jump.
Plan your bail-out point in advance so you never throw a good run chasing a bad idea.
Stop after two consecutive failures on the same section and come back fresh.
Clear a cool-down tower after a hard one to keep your hands and morale steady.

modules.name: The Eternal Abyss Warning Tags
modules.description: A reference for the warning hint printed on every The Eternal Abyss portal, explaining what each short tag promises about the tower behind it.

highlights.label: INCONSISTENT
highlights.detail: The tower changes rules and quality as you climb, so early jumps feel nothing like late ones.

highlights.label: LOOPFAILY
highlights.detail: Fails tend to send you back through content you already cleared, so memorization matters.

highlights.label: PUNISHING
highlights.detail: Mistakes are expensive, with tight timing and brutal fail states.

highlights.label: JANK
highlights.detail: The tower leans on engine quirks, odd hitboxes, and unconventional tech.

highlights.label: SCARY
highlights.detail: Tone and atmosphere carry the challenge rather than raw jump difficulty.

faq.title: The Eternal Abyss FAQ
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about The Eternal Abyss.

items.question: What is The Eternal Abyss?
items.answer: The Eternal Abyss is a high-difficulty Roblox tower obby by developer bLockerman666. You spawn into a main hub of 42 towers and climb roughly 10-floor obstacle courses through portals, with very little handholding and no penalty-free practice outside dedicated practice places.

items.question: Is The Eternal Abyss free to play?
items.answer: Yes. The Eternal Abyss is a free Roblox experience, so you only need a Roblox account to start climbing its towers.

items.question: How hard is The Eternal Abyss?
items.answer: The Eternal Abyss is deliberately brutal. The easiest content in its main area sits around the Insane tier, the community difficulty chart runs up to Nil, and the game states outright that losing progress is part of the deal.

items.question: Does The Eternal Abyss have codes?
items.answer: No active The Eternal Abyss codes are confirmed. The Eternal Abyss has no verified redemption system, so every reward in the game comes from clearing towers rather than entering codes.

items.question: Where should beginners start in The Eternal Abyss?
items.answer: Start in the main area and look for the single Non-Soul Crushing tower, which lets you respawn instead of wiping your progress. Warm up there and in a practice place before you attempt any Soul Crushing climb.

items.question: How many towers are in The Eternal Abyss?
items.answer: The namesake main area of The Eternal Abyss holds 42 towers, and the developer's goal is to reach 50 towers in each area. Timeless Manor adds 46 more, while Pit of Misery, Starry Night, and the upcoming Final Horizon expand the map further.
